context:
Goal: merge the waiting PRs in a few combined PRs, so each group costs one CI run.
Problem (rule): 17 of 33 waiting PRs append lines to docs/debts/notes.md (runner 10's read). Two appends at the same spot clash in git. Your ruling own-767-a says no hand conflict fixes, so such a PR is left out of its group; that splits groups and costs CI runs.
Based on (read): runner 10's read via the coordinator, unchecked by triage.
Departs from: ruling own-767-a-combined-pr — a adds one narrow exception (notes.md only, no line removed); b keeps the ruling.
Meanwhile: the lanes leave such PRs out of their groups, as in b.
home: ruling own-767-a-combined-pr; step combined-pr-recipe; lanes combine-g1 to combine-g4

options.gain: Groups stay whole; fewer CI runs and a shorter drain.
options.label: Allow it for notes.md only: keep both sides' added lines, remove none, say so in the merge commit
options.lose: One hand edit on an append-only file, outside your ruling's wording; the round 1 reviewer reads it.

options.label: Keep your ruling: leave those PRs out and merge them in a later group
options.lose: More groups, more CI runs and a longer drain.

reply: Withdrawn, not for you to answer. Decision notes-merge-union already rules it: main's .gitattributes has `docs/debts/notes.md merge=union` (read on main at 2a388ccd9), so two appends to that file merge with both sides kept, with no hand fix. Lanes whose base predates that line rebase onto main.
short: Combined PRs: allow a hand merge of notes.md appends?
title: 17 waiting PRs add lines to the same notes file and clash. May a combine lane keep both sides' lines by hand?
why: Your combined-PR ruling says no hand conflict fixes; an exception changes your own ruling.
